reason: Falsifier as written does not discriminate. Probe (n=17,l=6, pure numpy GF(2^17), 400 random 6-dim subspaces, exact sumset labels, y^2+xy=x^3+a6): natural SAT rate 0.78% (not a few %), so 4000 instances give ~31 positives; recall 0.99 is a 0-1 missed-positive event with no usable CI. Trivial baseline n_valid(V)=#x in V on curve (Tr(x+a6/x^3)=0), corr 0.997 with per-V SAT rate, alone gives instance-level AUC 0.569 > the 0.55 'false' threshold, so AUC in 0.55-0.75 is confounded by subspace point-count, not Weil-descent features. Degree-2 Macaulay rank deficit is constant by construction (d_ff=2, ffd_frobenius_witness mu=xR^-2 kills deg-2 part for every subspace; ffd_core run_cell semaev_ffd==null_ffd==2), zero-variance feature; trace-form invariants are functions of (V,xR,a6) = full input, label is membership of xR in a sumset of ~2^11 points among 2^17, i.e. pseudo-random set. No null arm specified beyond held-out subspaces. Cost metric 'saved ops' ill-defined: at n=17,l=6 exact solve is 2^6 enumeration or a 12-var F4, cheaper than any Macaulay rank feature, so net saving is negative by construction; toy cannot show scaling to n=131 (labels unobtainable there). Metric must be counted field-ops/F4 matrix entries, not wall time. Runnable in <20 CPU-min with python3+numpy (+msolve spot-check) once labels use sumset instead of msolve.
fix: Redesign: (1) Labels by exact sumset per subspace V (all 2^17 xR labelled at once from ~2^11 pair sums; cross-check 200 instances with msolve -g 2 / ic corpus .anf). (2) Sample >=20000 natural instances, 400+ subspaces, >=1500 positives; split GroupKFold by subspace AND by xR and curve a6 (x and -R share x; a6 shared). (3) Arms: A0 baseline = logistic on {n_valid(V), Tr class of xR, Tr(a6)}; A1 = A0 + deg-2 Macaulay rank deficit + deg-3 rank profile (deg-2 alone is constant, report its variance explicitly) + trace-form invariants; A2 null = same features computed on ffd_semaev_core.random_matched systems with shuffled labels within-subspace; A3 positive control = plant a label law (e.g. label := feature>thr) to prove pipeline detects AUC>=0.75; A4 oracle = per-V exact rate (upper bound for any V-only predictor). Claim 'true' only if A1 beats A0 by dAUC>=0.05 with bootstrap CI over subspaces excluding 0; 'false' if dAUC CI includes 0. (4) Metric: at recall 0.99 (report Clopper-Pearson lower bound given >=1500 positives) the UNSAT skip fraction s; net saving = s*C_solve - C_feat per instance, both in counted ops (GF(2^n) mults for enumeration solve and for GF(2) row-ops in rank features; F4 matrix entries from msolve -v 2 for the descended system), never wall time. (5) Scaling: repeat on grid n in {13,17,21,25}, l=(n-5)/2 (fixed SAT-rate ratio), fit s(n), dAUC(n), C_feat(n)/C_solve(n); extrapolation to n=131 is only a trend plus the argument that any n-independent s is a constant factor (<=m!) and any s->1 at poly cost would be a decomposability decision oracle ruled out by the generic bound S*T^2>=r/|Aut|. State plainly the toy is a trend test, not evidence for n=131. Expected outcome: dAUC~0 (A1 ~ A0 ~0.57), idea closes as relabelling of the point-count prior.
